newsitem.title: HUNGARY: PICK SAYS H1 SALES, PROFIT EXCEED PLANS.
newsitem.headline: PICK SAYS H1 SALES, PROFIT EXCEED PLANS.

text.p: Hungarian meat processor Pick Szeged Rt said on Monday that its sales and profit for the first half of 1997 were above plans.
"The pre-tax profit increase from the basis period (the first half of 1996) was 32.1 percent or 289 million forints," Pick said in its earnings report.
Pick's consolidated pre-tax profit in the first half of 1997 was 1.19 billion forints compared with 901 million forints in the same period of 1996 and a plan of 1.12 billion forints.
Pick said domestic sales of processed products rose in volume terms due to an increased presence in the cooperatives retail chain, supermarket chains and own retail outlets.
Export sales also were above both the respective figures of 1996 and plans, Pick said.
"Export sales grew above both the basis period and plans for the first half of this year due to prices, exchange rates, favourable product structure and a higher volume of dry products," Pick said.
It added that the sale of dry products was 113 tonnes higher than in the first half of 1996 and exports to Russia accounted for 60 tonnes of the increase.
Pick also said that the direct cost of sales, made up 70 percent of the purchase price of live hogs, was in line with plans but could rise further in the second half of 1997.
"The drop in supply already shows its effects in the third quarter and we expect higher average (purchase) prices for the second half," it said.
